title: Frequency To Musical Note Calculator
description: A three-octave keyboard strip highlighting the key nearest a chosen frequency, with note name, octave, exact frequency, and cents error. Keys are clickable and a sine oscillator sounds the selected frequency.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Music Technology
Peak Detection
chapter_title: Windowing, Spectral Leakage, and Peak Detection

educational.topic: Frequency to note conversion and cents error
learningObjectives: Calculate the nearest note and octave from a frequency
Compute cents deviation from the exact note frequency
Relate cents accuracy to required frequency resolution

controls.label: Piano keys
controls.action: Click a key to jump to its exact frequency and sound it; click anywhere off the keyboard to stop the tone

limitations: Frequency range is limited to the drawn keyboard, C3 (130.8 Hz) through B5 (987.8 Hz)
The tone is a pure sine wave with no harmonics, so it sounds unlike a real instrument at the same pitch
Audio requires a user gesture to start, per browser autoplay policy

keyQuestions: Why is a semitone a different number of Hertz at different pitches?
What frequency resolution does 5-cent accuracy require at A4?
commonMisconceptions: That notes are evenly spaced in Hertz
That identifying the nearest bin is accurate enough for tuning
assessmentOpportunities: Convert 329.0 Hz to a note and judge its acceptability
